title: Creating a Low-Cost RFID System with Business Central and Power Automate
summary: Building a low-cost RFID scan-in and scan-out system using an ESP32 microcontroller, PN532 RFID reader, Power Automate, and Business Central tables. The system captures location-based scans for resource tracking, automatically handles edge cases like forgotten scan-outs, and stores results in two related tables for monitoring.
key_points: Hardware uses ESP32 DEVKIT V1 and PN532 RFID scanner with I2C wiring on a breadboard, configured via web portal to connect to Power Automate
Power Automate acts as middleware between the ESP32 and Business Central, receiving JSON scan data and forwarding it via API
Business Central processes scans through two tables: ARD_Scans stores raw data, ARD_ScanTracker handles scan-in/out logic with automatic edge-case handling
When a tag scans at a new location without scanning out from the previous location, the system auto-completes the previous scan-out and flags it for review
Scan data flows from hardware to Power Automate HTTP trigger, then to Business Central API page, with an OnInsert trigger automating the scan logic

quotes.text: From this design the possibilities really open up. We can associate the RFID Tags with resources and track labor, or machine use time.
quotes.why_it_matters: Demonstrates extensibility potential for using the scan system beyond basic tracking, such as labor analytics and equipment utilization measurement
